site.name: ridenow-mobile
site.summary: ridenow-mobile Fictional rideshare app "RideNow" iOS-style mobile fixture. UXBench fixture in the Mobile Micro-UI category. Layout - 390 × 844 phone frame with chrome bezel, notch, status bar, home indicator - Bottom 4-tab bar: Ride / Activity / Payment / Account (Activity routes to the receipt screen) - Edge-to-edge on actual mobile (≤460 px) Screens (full ride flow) | `data-screen` | Highlights |

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full ridenow-mobile system, prioritizing the primary checkout/booking flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The mobile booking flow is generally understandable and visually coherent, with clear ride selection feedback and a functioning confirm action. However, several controls feel like dead ends or weak affordances on mobile, especially small top-bar icons, the Edit control, and some receipt feedback chips. The biggest issue is completion/recovery: the receipt state and fixed bottom navigation make it hard to reach or confidently use footer actions, while some tab actions don’t provide obvious feedback. Important untested areas remain, including several saved/place shortcuts and trip-management actions, so there may be additional interaction gaps outside the explored path.

exploration_plan.goal: Exhaustively explore the RideNow mobile booking flow from destination entry through ride setup and the adjacent Activity, Payment, and Account tabs, with attention to mobile-specific interaction issues and recovery behavior.
exploration_plan.summary: Start from the Ride tab and validate the primary booking path using the visible destination search, quick shortcuts, and recent/saved place selectors. Then branch into the bottom navigation tabs to inspect adjacent account, payment, and activity/receipt states, checking how the app handles navigation, state changes, and return paths. Repeat the most important interactions in mobile viewport to confirm the phone-frame experience and verify the small-tap-target warnings observed in the prescan.
assumptions: The fixture is a single-page app or single HTML entry with multiple in-app screens/states reachable via controls in index.html.
The 'Activity' tab routes to a receipt/completed-trip view, based on the prescan summary and visible headings.
The booking flow is likely driven by the 'Where to?' input plus quick destination buttons and arrow buttons on recent items.
risk_hotspots: Top-left menu (☰) and bell (🔔) buttons are below mobile tap-target guidance
Small right-arrow controls on recent place rows are below mobile tap-target guidance
Ride tab destination input ('Where to?') and its suggestion/transition behavior
Activity tab to receipt/completed-trip state routing
Payment and Account tabs for state persistence and unexpected navigation
Saved place/add place area for overflow, selection, or dead-end behavior

phases.title: Baseline ride screen and entry points
phases.objective: Confirm the default Ride screen structure and validate all visible entry points that can start or alter a booking.
key_checks: Inspect the default Ride screen layout in both desktop and mobile viewport.
Click the quick destination buttons: Home, Work, and PDX Airport.
Type into the 'Where to?' input and observe whether autocomplete, transition, or validation appears.
Open recent places using both the row body and the small right-arrow affordance if both are interactive.
Select saved places and the '+ Add place' control to see whether they open a detail, editor, or blocked state.
exit_criteria: All visible Ride-screen entry points have been exercised at least once.
Any navigation or state transition triggered by the destination controls has been observed.
The behavior of the destination input and recent/saved selectors is understood well enough to continue branching.

phases.title: Primary booking flow validation
phases.objective: Follow the most likely booking path from destination selection into any ride configuration or checkout steps exposed by the fixture.
key_checks: Use at least one quick destination and one typed destination to compare behavior.
Verify whether a ride options, fare, or confirmation state appears after destination selection.
Check whether any proceed/continue/confirm control becomes available after entering a destination.
Look for missing state resets or inconsistent back behavior when changing destinations mid-flow.
exit_criteria: The primary booking path has been exercised through its deepest reachable state.
Any confirmation, trip setup, or rate/receipt-related handoff is documented.
No additional booking controls remain untested on the Ride screen.

phases.title: Activity and receipt/completion flow
phases.objective: Validate the adjacent Activity route and the completed-trip/receipt experience called out in the prescan.
key_checks: Open the Activity tab from the bottom navigation.
Confirm whether it routes to a Trip complete, Rate your driver, or Receipt state.
Inspect any receipt details, rating controls, and return navigation from that state.
Verify whether Activity preserves or clears ride context when coming from the booking screen.
exit_criteria: The Activity route and its terminal states have been reached.
Any rating or receipt-related controls have been checked.
Return/back behavior from the Activity/receipt state has been observed.

phases.title: Payment and account area checks
phases.objective: Inspect the non-booking tabs for consistency, navigation reliability, and any configuration or profile state.
key_checks: Open the Payment tab and inspect available payment methods or settings.
Open the Account tab and inspect profile, preferences, or account-related content.
Check whether Payment and Account share persistent UI state or reset the current ride context.
Test whether switching between tabs causes unexpected blank states or layout shifts.
exit_criteria: Both Payment and Account tabs have been opened and reviewed.
Any settings or account controls visible in those tabs have been exercised.
Tab switching behavior is confirmed stable enough for the run to proceed.

phases.title: Mobile viewport and interaction risk review
phases.objective: Repeat the highest-value interactions in mobile viewport and verify the fixture’s known mobile usability risks.
key_checks: Repeat destination selection and at least one tab switch in mobile viewport.
Tap the small top-left menu, bell, and right-arrow controls to confirm hit-area usability and whether any mis-taps occur.
Check that the bottom tab bar remains usable and visually stable within the phone frame.
Confirm the screen does not introduce clipping, overlap, or unexpected scrolling in mobile mode.
exit_criteria: Critical booking and navigation interactions have been validated in mobile viewport.
The small tap-target risks have been directly exercised.
No additional mobile-specific layout or interaction defects are left unreviewed.

coverage_targets.pages: visit all known HTML pages; in this fixture that means fully exercising index.html and all in-app states reachable from it
coverage_targets.features: exercise most visible controls on Ride, plus the bottom tabs, destination input, quick destinations, recent places, saved places, and add-place control
coverage_targets.mobile: repeat the primary booking path and at least one tab-switch path in mobile viewport, with explicit attention to the known small tap targets

notes: Because only one HTML file is known, coverage should focus on in-app state breadth rather than page count.
The small tap-target warnings are low severity but should be validated because they affect core mobile navigation controls.

findings.user_goal: Finish a ride and confirm the trip is complete or dismissed
findings.problem: The receipt/completion flow is visually clipped on mobile and the bottom navigation overlaps the lower part of the content, making the Done action hard or impossible to reach from the observed state.
findings.evidence: In the mobile receipt state, the bottom tab bar is pinned over the lower receipt area; the 'Done' button is reported below the viewport (bbox y 928), and scroll only moved slightly (y 82→92).
findings.why_it_matters: If users cannot reliably reach the completion button, they may feel trapped on the receipt screen or be unable to exit the post-trip flow cleanly.
findings.suggestion: Move the receipt footer above the tab bar, add bottom padding, or make the completion action sticky and always visible above the fixed nav.

findings.user_goal: Know what happens after tapping post-trip tabs and actions
findings.problem: Several important actions on the receipt screen do not provide visible feedback, including Activity tab taps and the share/export icon, so users get no confirmation that anything happened.
findings.evidence: Activity tab click did not visibly change the screen in some states, and tapping the receipt share/export icon produced no visible state change, modal, sheet, or text update.
findings.why_it_matters: When users tap a control and nothing appears to happen, they may repeat taps, lose confidence, or assume the app is broken.
findings.suggestion: Provide immediate visual feedback for tab switches and share actions, such as loading state, active-state change, toast, or a native share sheet.
findings.source_hint: index.html / bottom tabs and receipt share icon

findings.user_goal: Modify trip details or adjust the booking before confirming
findings.problem: The Edit control is extremely small on mobile and appears non-responsive, with no visible change after tapping it.
findings.evidence: The Edit button is only 37×18 px and the click caused no URL, text, or screen change; the view remained on the ride-selection screen with no exposed edit surface.
findings.why_it_matters: Users who need to correct pickup details or adjust the booking may not discover how to do so, especially on a phone where small controls are easy to miss.
findings.suggestion: Enlarge the Edit affordance, make it clearly button-like, and open a visible edit sheet or inline form when tapped.

findings.user_goal: Open navigation, alerts, or other top-bar utilities
findings.problem: The compact top-bar icons, especially the menu and bell, are small and gave no visible feedback when tapped, making them feel like dead-end controls.
findings.evidence: The hamburger and bell are 42×42 px, below the 44 px mobile guidance, and clicks produced no visible state change, route change, or notification surface.
findings.why_it_matters: Small, inert-looking controls reduce discoverability and can make core navigation utilities feel unreliable on mobile.
findings.suggestion: Increase hit area, add clearer active/pressed states, and ensure each icon opens an obvious surface or feedback state.

findings.user_goal: Use the app comfortably on a phone without mis-taps
findings.problem: Multiple tappable elements fall below recommended mobile touch sizes, including top-bar icons, back arrows, the Edit control, and some post-trip chips.
findings.evidence: Observed tap-target warnings include 42×42 px menu/bell, 32×28 px arrows, 32×32 back/share icons, 37×18 Edit, and 74×27 to 103×27 chips.
findings.why_it_matters: Small targets increase accidental taps and make the interface harder to use for everyone, especially on smaller screens or for users with motor impairments.
findings.suggestion: Increase minimum touch areas to at least 44×44 px and add spacing around dense controls, especially in the header and receipt area.
findings.source_hint: index.html / top bar, arrows, receipt chips

findings.user_goal: See whether a feedback chip or star rating selection was registered
findings.problem: Post-trip feedback controls show weak or no immediate selection feedback, so users may not know whether their rating choice was saved.
findings.evidence: Clicking the star rating produced no obvious visible state change, and tapping the 'Great driving' and 'Quiet ride' chips produced no visible text/URL change or selection change.
findings.why_it_matters: If rating inputs don’t confirm selection, users may abandon the feedback step or submit the wrong choice.
findings.suggestion: Show a clear selected state, success acknowledgment, or lightweight confirmation when a rating chip or star is chosen.
findings.source_hint: index.html / rating area on receipt screen

findings.user_goal: Move between primary app sections from the bottom tabs
findings.problem: Bottom navigation is inconsistent in its response across states, with some tab taps visibly switching screens and others showing no clear change.
findings.evidence: Ride tab visibly changed the screen to the Ride home flow, but Payment and Activity taps were reported as having no visible change in some explored states.
findings.why_it_matters: Inconsistent tab behavior creates uncertainty about whether the user is in the right place and whether the app preserved context.
findings.suggestion: Make each tab switch produce a consistent active-state update and clear content transition, or disable tabs that are unavailable in the current state.

findings.user_goal: Understand what the small arrow beside a recent place does
findings.problem: The compact arrow control changes content in place, but its purpose is not obvious and it doesn’t clearly indicate selection or a detail state.
findings.evidence: Tapping the arrow produced visible content change, yet the screen did not show a distinct detail view or explicit feedback explaining the arrow’s purpose, and the Ride option remained highlighted.
findings.why_it_matters: Ambiguous disclosure controls can make users hesitate or tap the wrong part of the row, especially on mobile.
findings.suggestion: Label the action more clearly or use a clearer chevron/expansion pattern that shows whether it opens details, selects the row, or advances the flow.

findings.user_goal: Know whether tapping Add place will do anything useful
findings.problem: The '+ Add place' control appears to be a dead end from the observed states, with no visible feedback after tapping and a vague label that does not explain the outcome.
findings.evidence: Clicking '+ Add place' produced no visible UI change, no modal/sheet, and no feedback; the label only says 'Up to 8 saved.'
findings.why_it_matters: Users may not understand whether this is an actionable control, a limit note, or an unavailable feature.
findings.suggestion: Use a clearer verb phrase and open an obvious add-place editor or sheet when tapped.

findings.user_goal: Exit the receipt screen and return to booking
findings.problem: The Done action appears to return users abruptly to the Ride/home surface without an explicit success or completion acknowledgement.
findings.evidence: Clicking Done changed visible content, but it returned to the Ride/home state rather than showing a confirmation, success message, or receipt-dismiss state.
findings.why_it_matters: Users may wonder whether the receipt was saved, whether the trip ended, or whether they accidentally backed out of something important.
findings.suggestion: Show a brief confirmation or success state before returning to the main ride screen, so completion feels intentional.
